source.title: The Feynman integral path a Henstock integral: a survey and open problems

accepted.question_text: Let ψ(ξ,τ) be the Feynman state function defined as a Henstock integral over the path space R^T, namely ψ(ξ,τ)=∫_{R^T} exp(-i∫_T V(x(t),t)dt) exp((i/2)∫_T (dx/dt)^2 dt) ∏_{t∈T} δx(x)/√(2πi dt). If the interaction factor exp(-i∫_T V(x(t),t)dt) is expanded into its power series, can one rigorously interchange the infinite series with the Henstock path integral in equation (6.2), so that ψ = Σ_{r=0}^∞ ψ_r and the Feynman-diagram expansion is mathematically justified?
accepted.context_brief: Interchanging the Henstock path integral and perturbation series

evidence.quote: Assuming that we can interchange the order of the integral and the series in the expression (6.2) (this is assumed in the Perturbation Theory, see [22]), then ψ = P∞ r=0 ψr

On the other hand, we would like to justify formally the exchange of integral and series in (6.2). However, we try to prove that with the mathematical tool that gives us the integral of Henstock there are difficulties and it is not possible to make this justification.
to our knowledge, the mathematical instruments seem to be not enough to justify particular applications as Feynman’s diagrams.

accepted.question_text: Let g0(x,N,I[N]) be the free-particle Fresnel integrand and let β(x,N,I[N]) be the positive integrable majorant required by bounded convergence for Henstock integration on R^T. Suppose E is a Banach space equipped with a cone P that defines a partial order, and that both |g0| and β belong to E. In the case where β ≤ |g0| for every γ0-fine associated triple (equivalently, |g0|−β ∈ P), can one introduce a suitable supremum notion in E and use it to obtain the contradiction needed to analyze whether the Henstock path integral can be exchanged with the perturbation series?
accepted.context_brief: Cone and supremum approach in a Banach space

evidence.quote: In the case that, |g0|−β ∈ P for each γ0−fine (x, N, I[N]) implies that β ≤ |g0|, for every γ0−fine (x, N, I[N]), here we need to introduce the supremum in Banach spaces in order to give a contradiction.
This case is being analyzed with supremum concept.

accepted.question_text: For the function space H = { h : R^T × N(T) × I(R^T) → C : |∫_{R^T} h| < ∞ }, what is its size as a vector space? More specifically, can one prove that the cardinality of H is at most the continuum c, and therefore that the vector-space dimension of H is exactly c?

evidence.quote: We consider important to study properties of the function space H = { h : RT × N (T ) × I(RT ) → C : |∫RT h| < ∞ }.
We would like to show that Card(H) ≤ c, then Dim(H) = c.

accepted.question_text: The paper cites a result asserting that the function space H of Henstock-integrable path-space integrands carries a Banach space structure. Is the norm that gives H this Banach space structure induced by the Henstock integral itself?
accepted.context_brief: Whether the Banach norm on H comes from the integral

evidence.quote: By [28, Corollary 2.4] it is provided of a Banach space structure to H. We do not know if this norm is induced by the integral.

accepted.question_text: For the function space H of Henstock-integrable functions on path space R^T, does the known theorem that there is no natural Banach space norm on Henstock integrable functions from R^n to R extend to H as well?
accepted.context_brief: Extending the no-natural-Banach-norm result to H

evidence.quote: in the case Rn, it is possible to show that there exists no natural Banach space norm on Henstock integrable functions over Rn to R, see [27, Theorem 2.7], which makes us think that this result can be extended over H
